note: SYNTHETIC prototype policy set for demonstration. It does not reproduce any real company's policy. Definitions are deliberately high level and never describe harmful content. Contacts are roles, not people.

policies.name: Child safety
policies.definition: Content or behaviour that sexualises, endangers or exploits minors.
signals: Specialist verdict on a child-safety policy area
policies.severity_guidance: Confirmed violation: P0. Any credible signal: at least P1. Mandatory specialist review always; auto-pause applies at P0.
checklist: Review only the restricted summary fields; never reproduce content
Confirm or lift the automatic pause
Decide whether account action is needed (Incident Lead approval)
Legal/Privacy decides on mandatory external reporting

policies.name: CBRN weapons uplift
policies.definition: Meaningful assistance towards chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons.
signals: Specialist verdict on a CBRN policy area
policies.severity_guidance: Confirmed uplift: P0. Blocked or refused attempt: P2-P3 unless repeated or coordinated. Mandatory specialist review; auto-pause applies at P0.
escalation: Incident Lead (P0, classifier and account actions)
checklist: Check whether the model provided content or refused (classifier action)
Confirm or lift the automatic pause
Consider a classifier block rule (Incident Lead approval)
Check for related reports from the same actor

policies.name: Self-harm & suicide
policies.definition: Responses that encourage or facilitate self-harm or suicide, or fail a user at risk.
signals: Specialist verdict on a self-harm policy area
policies.severity_guidance: Harmful response to a user at risk: P1. Pattern across users: P0. Mandatory specialist review.
checklist: Check whether safe-messaging resources were shown
Assess whether the user may still be at risk
Look for the same failure on other conversations
Route model fix to Model Behavior

policies.name: Violent extremism & threats
policies.definition: Support for violent extremist groups, credible threats of violence, or incitement.
policies.severity_guidance: Credible imminent threat: P0. Propaganda or support content: P1. Mandatory specialist review.
checklist: Assess credibility and imminence of any threat
Check for linked accounts or coordinated activity
Decide on account action (Incident Lead)
Legal/Privacy decides on any referral

policies.name: Over-refusal / enforcement appeal
policies.definition: A user or customer disputes a refusal or enforcement action as wrong.
signals: Appeal or complaint about a refusal
policies.severity_guidance: Usually P2-P3. P1 if a business-critical customer workflow is blocked.
checklist: Check whether the refusal matched policy
Look for the same false positive elsewhere
Agree the customer response with Enterprise/CS

policies.name: Influence operations
policies.definition: Coordinated, deceptive use of the product to manipulate public opinion or elections.
signals: Many linked accounts with similar content
policies.severity_guidance: Active coordinated campaign: P1. Election-period or large scale: P0.
checklist: Map the linked accounts and shared signals
Decide on rate limits or account action (Incident Lead)
Preserve evidence for any public disclosure

policies.name: Fraud & scams
policies.definition: Use of the product to defraud, impersonate or scam people at scale.
policies.severity_guidance: Active scam at scale: P1. Single attempt, blocked: P3.
checklist: Check volume and whether harm reached victims
Look for linked accounts
Decide on account action

policies.name: Cyber offense
policies.definition: Meaningful assistance with malware, intrusion or other offensive cyber operations.
signals: Malicious code or intrusion help requested
policies.severity_guidance: Working offensive capability provided: P1, P0 if used in an active attack. Refused attempt: P3.
escalation: Product Security (if our systems are involved)
checklist: Check whether usable capability was provided
Check for an active attack or victim
Decide on classifier or account action

policies.name: Deepfake / NCII
policies.definition: Non-consensual intimate imagery or deceptive synthetic media of real people.
signals: Image generation of a real, identifiable person
policies.severity_guidance: Generated intimate imagery of a real person: P1. Shared or targeted at the victim: P0.
checklist: Confirm what was generated without reproducing it
Support the victim's removal request
Decide on account action

policies.name: Jailbreak / safeguard bypass
policies.definition: Techniques that reliably get the model to ignore its safety training.
policies.severity_guidance: Universal bypass reaching a severe policy area: P1. Narrow bypass: P2.
escalation: Safety specialist (if severe areas are reachable)
checklist: Reproduce in a controlled environment
Check which policy areas the bypass reaches
Consider a classifier block while a model fix is made

policies.name: Enterprise data leakage
policies.definition: Customer or company data exposed outside its intended audience, including across tenants.
signals: Share or export to an external audience
policies.severity_guidance: Confirmed exposure of sensitive data: P0. Possible exposure, unconfirmed: P1.
checklist: Establish who could access the data and whether they did
Contain the exposure (e.g. disable a connector)
Legal/Privacy decides on notification
Agree the customer message

policies.name: Privacy / PII exposure
policies.definition: Personal information about a person revealed, retained or inferred without a valid reason.
signals: Model reveals someone else's personal data
policies.severity_guidance: Another person's sensitive data revealed: P0-P1. Own data, unexpected: P2.
checklist: Identify whose data and how it was reached
Contain the data path
Legal/Privacy decides on notification

policies.name: Prompt injection & agent hijacking
policies.definition: Untrusted content instructs the model or agent to act against the user.
signals: Instructions hidden in a document, web page or email
Data sent to an unknown destination
policies.severity_guidance: Secrets or data exfiltrated: P0. Hijack without harm: P1-P2.
checklist: Identify the injected source
Rotate any exposed credentials (Incident Lead)
Isolate untrusted instructions in the affected tool

policies.name: Model / secret leakage
policies.definition: Exposure of system prompts, credentials, model internals or other secrets.
policies.severity_guidance: Live credentials exposed: P0. Non-sensitive internals: P2-P3.
checklist: Check whether anything exposed is still valid
Rotate secrets if needed
Fix the leak path

policies.name: Agentic overreach
policies.definition: An agent acts beyond what the user asked or approved (files, payments, messages).
policies.severity_guidance: Irreversible harm (deleted data, money moved): P1. Reversible: P2.
checklist: Confirm what the user approved
Check whether the action can be reversed
Require confirmation for the risky action type

policies.name: Harmful inaccuracy
policies.definition: Confidently wrong information in a domain where it can cause real harm (medical, legal, financial).
policies.severity_guidance: Risk of physical harm: P1. Otherwise P2-P3.
checklist: Reproduce and check against an authoritative source
Look for the same error elsewhere
Route the fix to Model Behavior

policies.name: Bias & discrimination
policies.definition: Outputs that treat people unfairly based on protected characteristics.
policies.severity_guidance: Used in a consequential decision (hiring, lending): P1. Otherwise P2-P3.
checklist: Reproduce across comparable inputs
Check whether it affected a real decision
Agree the customer response

policies.name: Product failure
policies.definition: A product defect or outage without a policy violation.
policies.severity_guidance: Usually P2-P3. P1 if many customers are blocked.
checklist: Reproduce
Check scope
Route to the owning engineering team

policies.name: No policy issue
policies.definition: No evidence of a policy violation or product harm (confusion, duplicates, expected behaviour).
checklist: Confirm nothing was missed
Reply to the reporter
Link duplicates
